submission.natural_language_explanation: A lexical (token-identity) detector in layer 1: it fires on a small fixed set of word-initial tokens, strongest on ' Focus' (any sense, especially the brand/name), ' carry' (base form only; ' carried' is weak), ' Mass'/' MA', ' inst', ' wave', ' influence' used as a verb, ' subject', ' attent/attention', ' FM', ' Tanzania', plus 'urch' right after a line-initial 'P' (Purchasing) and ' office' only right after ' box'. Synonyms and close variants of these words (spread, affect, topic, light, care, carried, the noun 'influence', ' office' without 'box') stay weak or inactive, so the activation is set by the current token's identity plus at most the one token before it, not by meaning.

rival_explanations: Semantic reading: the pole fires on words for acts of transferring or affecting (carry, influence, purchase, install, feed, spread, transmit, shape), an 'act/event' concept, so any such verb should activate it moderately regardless of exact token.

Context-insensitive unigram reading: the pole is a pure lookup on the current token id, so ' office', ' influence' and 'urch' should activate equally in every context (e.g. 'The office was closed' as strongly as 'The box office was closed').
